userStories.title: The U48-5 flush-pair measurement gate — build, run, report the number
userStories.evidence: WITHIN THRESHOLD: 25/327 flush pairs lose drill-in (7.6 %) vs stop line 109. Corpus 721 / flush 327 (R42-D1: 628 / 324) calibration reported. 14-assertion selftest, --plant RED (3 assertions), corpus-level control (band 40 → 72.5 %). Own port :3100 --strictPort, no sidecar, ports freed. Number written into plan §3.9/§9 by the lead; committed with the spike files.
acceptanceCriteria: .omc/spikes/phase48-model/flush-pairs.mjs exists and computes, for a corpus of nested parent/child [data-oid] pairs with their layout rects, (a) the flush relation, (b) for each flush pair, the parent's eight C48-1 regions via the SPIKE's handleRegions with DEFAULT_HANDLE_GEOMETRY, (c) whether the child's box minus every parent resize region has an inscribed disc of radius ≥ 4 (the spike's certified purchase measure applied to that residual region) — 'loses drill-in' per plan §3.9.

A driver collects the corpus from the RUNNING dogfood app's DOM (every screen route under src/app/** the extractor knows), on a port the lane owns; the owner's :3000/:3001/:7331 servers are never killed or reused; the sidecar :7331 is never started by the lane if it is already bound.

The flush definition used is stated with its tolerance, and the corpus size and flush count are reported beside R42-D1's recorded 628 / 324 (51.6 %) as a calibration — a disagreement is reported, not hidden.

The count of flush pairs losing drill-in is reported to the LEAD in the final message with the command that reproduces it; if it exceeds one third of the flush population, the report says STOP AND REPORT TO THE OWNER in its first line.
The instrument has a control: a synthetic pair known to lose drill-in (a child thinner than 10 px flush on one side) and one known to keep it are both classified correctly, evidence pasted.
The lane does NOT write into the plan (S48-0a owns .omc/plans); the lead writes the number into §3.9/§9 after S48-0a lands.
